latin.659: §. VIII. Secunda Probatio Autoris, quâ Oralem Manducationem, fundamento fidei innexam, in Anti-Irenico suo Tractatu docuerat, à SOLO SUCCO SOLATII petita erat, in hac Manducatione ab eo quæsito repositóque; Cùm verò Succum hunc ex Orali Manducatione haudquaquam fluere per id ostendissem, quòd hæc impiis, seu indignè manducantibus, ex hypothesi Autoris, communis est, ne guttulam quidem solatii, nedum integrum succum suppeditatura.
latin.660: Autor subodoratus, Oralem Manducationem succi solatii fontem nativum esse haud posse, non de sola Manducatione orali, vel indignorum, sed ipsâ etiam Corp. & Sang. Christi in Cœna præsentia, verâque sacramentali Manducatione, inter nos disputari ait §. XVI. Sed verò corpus Christi vivificare Joh. 6, 53. Sanguinem etiam Christi à peccatorum sordibus purgare, indeque simulac utrumque manducantibus & bibentibus verè distribuitur, latentem quoque in utroque succum solatii, iisdem propinari, pertendit ibidem, hocque ipsum unô alióque Simili illustrat, donec tandem ita concludat: Tantum, inquit, (Solatii) in Orali Manducatione Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, & quam illa supponit, vera & reali præsentia, situm est, ut scil. ubi mediantibus pane & vino, Christum ipsum nos participare, (puta oraliter) meminimus, tùm verò præ nimio gaudio, Evolemus, Evolemus, cum Monica, Hipponensi matre, intra nos exclamemus, Parag. XVI.
latin.661: Respondeo (1) Bene habet, quòd Autor soli Manducationi corporis Christi Orali in tantum non fidit, ut succum solatii ab ea dependere arbitretur, præsentiam potiùs veram corporis & sanguinis Christi huc arcessat, & ab hac, eóque ab ipso corpore & sanguine Christi succum solatii omnem derivet; Sed perperam, & hîc, & alibi, tùm suprâ, tùm infrà, non de sola Manducatione Orali & Indignorum, sed de ipsâ etiam præsentia, & vera Sacramentali Manducatione, nos inter disputari arguit; id quod retrò Præceptori suo Danhauer o castigandum commisimus, nunquam & nusquam de præsentia corporis Christi, vel de vera sacramentali Manducatione, Spiritualibus puta, cum quoquam Lutheranorum, disceptaturi, oblocuturi interim perpetuò tùm Corporali indeque locali & naturali præsentiæ, tùm Orali, eóque eatenus & naturali & carnali Manducationi corporis Christi, sive à Lutherano, sive ab alio quocunque doceatur.
latin.662: (2) Dum carni & sanguini Christi, vel extra Cœnam S., vel in ipsâ Cœna, præsentibus, vivificatio & à sordibus peccatorum purgatio indeque manducantibus utrumque, & bibentibus solatii succus, ab istis oriundus, transscribitur, non aliis certè manducantibus ac bibentibus transscribendus censebitur, quàm Spiritualiter manducantibus & bibentibus, reliquis & citra manducationem & bibitionem Spiritualem manducantibus & bibentibus, omnis solatii, nedum succi hujus, expertibus omnino. Ut sic clarissimè intelligatur, succum solatii non ex Manducatione corporis Christi Orali, sed Spirituali profluere, neque oraliter, sed spiritualiter demum manducantes, præ nimio gaudio animi sui spiritualis, intra se, cum Monica, exclamare posse: Evolemus Evolemus. Vel cum integro potiùs piorum & dignè Christo communicantium Cœtu, apud Esaiam cap. 61. præ gaudio intonare: Omnino gaudeo in Jehova. Sc. Postquam jussus edere, auscultavi Domino, & comedi bonum & oblectata est anima mea. Esa. 55, 2. coll. cum 1. Cor. 10, 3. 4.
latin.663: §. IX. Tertia Autoris Probatio, Negantibus Oralem Manducationem, Communionis Sanctorum negationem imputaverat, Symbolo tamen Christianorum communi, seu Apostolicô traditæ; sic facilè evictura, de Fundamentali articulo disceptari, dum de Orali Manducatione serra Disputationis reciprocature. Quando verò ego regesseram: Communionem Sanctorum orali manducatione haud causari, nisi & impios Communioni huic immisceri velimus, non minus ac pios sanctósque, ex hypothesi Lutherana, Oraliter manducantes.
latin.664: Autor rursus initio paragraphi XVII. à Manducatione Orali, inter nos disputabili, ad commentitiam de præsentia corporis Christi in Cœna ejusque Sacramentali verâque & reali Manducatione, disputationem relabitur, hîc præsidium suum unicum quæsiturus; & quoniam corporis Christi præsentia in Cœna, hujusque sacramentalis vera ac realis Manducatio, Communioni Sanctorum analoga est, se jam tum omne id confecisse sibi persuadet, quod intenderat, haud memor, tùm Præsentiam corporis Christi, in Cœna, tùm Manducationem Sacramentalem veram realémque, sed utramque Spiritualem, à Reformatis constantissimè doceri: quæ interim sola, non verò Oralis, Communionis Sanctorum in Symbolo Apostolico celebratæ, Articulóque de Ecclesia Catholica contradistinctæ, fons audit & scaturigo. Hinc præter rem h. l. inter Communionem Externam, & Internam, discriminat Auctor; quando prior Sanctorum non est, quatenus sancti sunt, sed ad Ecclesiam Catholicam pertinet, in qua sancti, & immundi hypocritæ, juxta continentur, non autem juxta Sanctorum Communione strictè sic dictâ & interna fruuntur.

pass_a.659: §. VIII. The Author’s Second Proof, by which in his Anti-Irenic Tract he had taught Oral Eating bound to the foundation of faith, was sought from the JUICE OF SOLACE ALONE, sought and placed by him in this Eating; But when I had shown that this Juice in no way flows from Oral Eating by this — that this Eating, on the Author’s hypothesis, is common to the impious or those eating unworthily, and so will supply not even a drop of solace, much less the whole juice.
pass_a.660: The Author, scenting that Oral Eating can hardly be the native fountain of the juice of solace, says in §. XVI that the dispute between us is not about Oral Eating alone, or that of the unworthy, but also about the very presence of Christ’s Body and Blood in the Supper, and true sacramental Eating. But indeed that Christ’s body vivifies (John 6:53), and also that Christ’s Blood purges from the filth of sins, and thence as soon as either is truly distributed to those eating and drinking, the juice of solace latent in either is also offered to them, he presses in the same place, and illustrates this very thing with one and another Simile, until at last he concludes thus: So much (of Solace), he says, is situated in the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body and Blood, and in the true and real presence which that Eating suppose, that namely when by means of bread and wine we remember that we participate Christ Himself (namely oraliter), then indeed from too much joy we cry within ourselves with Monica, mother of Hippo: Let us fly away, Let us fly away — Parag. XVI.
pass_a.661: I reply (1) It is well that the Author does not so far trust the Oral Eating of Christ’s body alone as to judge the juice of solace to depend on it — rather he fetches hither the true presence of Christ’s body and blood, and from this, and so from Christ’s body and blood themselves, derives every juice of solace; But wrongly, both here and elsewhere, above and below, he argues that the dispute between us is not about Oral Eating and that of the Unworthy alone, but also about presence itself and true Sacramental Eating — which thing we formerly committed to his Preceptor Danhauer to chastise: we are never and nowhere about to dispute with any of the Lutherans about the presence of Christ’s body, or about true sacramental Eating, namely the Spiritual — meantime forever to speak against both the Corporal and thence local and natural presence, and the Oral, and so far also natural and carnal Eating of Christ’s body, whether taught by a Lutheran or by any other whoever.
pass_a.662: (2) While vivification and purgation from the filth of sins, and thence the juice of solace arising from these for those eating either and drinking, is ascribed to Christ’s flesh and blood present either outside the Sacred Supper or in the Supper itself, it will certainly be judged to be ascribed to no other eaters and drinkers than those eating and drinking Spiritually — the rest who eat and drink also apart from Spiritual eating and drinking being altogether without all solace, much less this juice. So that it may be understood most clearly that the juice of solace flows not from the Oral Eating of Christ’s body but from the Spiritual, and that not those eating oraliter but those finally eating spiritualiter can cry within themselves with Monica from the too-great joy of their spiritual soul: Let us fly away, Let us fly away. Or rather with the whole Company of the pious and those worthily communicating with Christ, thunder for joy at Isaiah ch. 61: I altogether rejoice in Jehovah. Namely: After I was commanded to eat, I hearkened to the Lord, and I ate the good, and my soul was delighted. Isa. 55:2, collated with 1 Cor. 10:3–4.
pass_a.663: §. IX. The Author’s Third Proof had imputed to those denying Oral Eating a negation of the Communion of Saints, handed down yet in the Christians’ common Symbol, or the Apostolic; thus easily about to prove that a Fundamental article is being disputed while the saw of Disputation is reciprocated about Oral Eating. But when I had retorted: That the Communion of Saints is hardly caused by oral eating, unless we also wish the impious mixed into this Communion no less than the pious and holy, who on the Lutheran hypothesis eat Oraliter.
pass_a.664: The Author again at the start of paragraph XVII slides back from the Oral Eating disputable between us to the fabricated dispute about the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper and its true and real Sacramental Eating, about to seek his only stronghold here; and since the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper, and this sacrament’s true and real Eating, is analogous to the Communion of Saints, he persuades himself he has already then accomplished all he intended — not remembering that both the Presence of Christ’s body in the Supper and true real Sacramental Eating, but each Spiritual, are most constantly taught by the Reformed: which meantime alone, not the Oral, is heard as the fountain and spring of the Communion of Saints celebrated in the Apostolic Symbol and contradistinguished from the Article on the Catholic Church. Hence beside the point in this place the Author discriminates between External and Internal Communion; when the prior is not of the Saints inasmuch as they are holy, but pertains to the Catholic Church, in which saints and unclean hypocrites are contained alike, yet they do not alike enjoy the Saints’ Communion strictly so called and internal.

659: §.VIII: the Author’s second Anti-Irenic proof tied Oral eating to the faith-foundation by the juice of solace alone sought in that eating.
Strimesius had shown that juice cannot flow from Oral — on the Author’s own hypothesis Oral is common to the unworthy, so it yields not even a drop of solace.
660: Sensing that, the Author (§.XVI) claims the dispute is not Oral alone but also presence of body and blood and true sacramental eating — body vivifies (Jn 6:53), blood purges, and solace-juice is offered with them.
He ends with Monica of Hippo: when we remember we orally participate Christ through bread and wine, we cry within from joy — Evolemus, Evolemus.
661: Reply (1): good that he will not hang solace on Oral alone but fetches true presence — yet he wrongly says we also dispute presence and true sacramental (spiritual) eating.

As with Danhauer: we never dispute spiritual presence or spiritual sacramental eating with Lutherans; we forever oppose corporal/local/natural presence and oral/natural/carnal eating of Christ’s body.
662: Reply (2): vivification, purgation, and solace-juice belong only to those who eat and drink spiritually — others who eat without spiritual eating have no solace at all.

So the juice flows from Spiritual eating, not Oral. Only spiritual eaters can cry Evolemus with Monica — or with Isaiah’s company rejoice in Jehovah after eating the good (Isa. 55:2; 1 Cor. 10:3–4). Stop §.VIII before §.IX.
663: §.IX: third proof — denying Oral is charged as denying the Communion of Saints in the Apostles’ Creed, hence a fundamental article.
Strimesius had retorted: oral eating does not cause that Communion unless the impious are mixed in with the holy — since on the Lutheran hypothesis the unworthy also eat orally.
664: The Author (§.XVII) again slides from Oral to a fabricated fight over presence and true real sacramental eating as his only stronghold — forgetting the Reformed constantly teach both as Spiritual.

Spiritual presence/eating alone is the fountain of the Creed’s Communion of Saints (vs the Catholic Church article). External church communion holds saints and hypocrites together; internal Saints’ communion they do not share alike. Stop before §.X.
